On reflection… I think it’s because …….the absolute beauty and wonder and tranquility of the images are so able to capture American beauty and therefore make one patriotic and proud and even nostalgic for those days. And yet I knew….i knew…. I knew… those days are gone. They are gone because of Republican politics.

Trump is a child raping draft dodger. 

Americans don’t care.

If he’s their Republican, they’ll vote for him.

And here we are. An administration that is so astonishingly corrupt and disgusting that the world has changed forever.

So if you’re wondering why my comment is relevant to this beautiful, beautiful video, I answer this way: it is entirely relevant because the actual world actually could be like this. We could have snowy Christmasases, and in-polluted beaches and peace and equality and so on. But I can’t enjoy this syrupy version of non- reality because, well, we acquiesce to a dozen or so murdering humans that put our young men and women in uniform and pay them
well enough to do so - order that they’ll follow orders.
To bomb actual children in schools in Iran.

The USA: you are not a romantic, beautiful autumn scene. You could be. But you are not.
You are a disgusting mirror in the face if the worst of humanity.

@GilbertM3 Late Sept to early October is mid-full peak fall foliage in New England this year. This reminds me of Acorn St. in Beacon Hill neighborhood in Boston. Google Acorn St. It's the most American street in America. Boston in the fall is the BEST! Beacon Hill, Back Bay, North End, Charlestown, Harvard Square in Cambridge. I lived there for nine years and miss it so much. Go! Enjoy! :-)
At first glance, I thought it was real, but then was like...no, gotta be Ai?

@The479Angie It's definitely AI-ified, but you would be surprised how closely some New England towns and streets look like this. It's the thing I miss most about living there. Acorn St. in Beacon Hill in Boston even had a golden retriever named Callie that napped outside one of the brownstones and the internet mourned when she died! You walk down that street in peak fall and think, "This can't be real."
America at its peak.
